answer: At each epoch's dawn, the network posts 20 admission probes, each paying one winner only. A candidate must solve a probe with a fresh, never-winning key, then post a 500-token bond; a key winning twice, or two answers over 0.95 similar within 30 seconds, gets both bonds burned by a 2/3 validator quorum replaying the check on-chain. A farmer pays 500 tokens plus compute per fresh identity, cannot reuse keys, and cannot parallelize past the 20-probe supply, so marginal cost is linear in n: each clone is another pearl bought at full price, keeping the haven against farms.
